When Someone You Love Is Dying

For the weeks when someone you love is dying and nothing prepares you. It asks the team what to expect, gets their wishes written down, splits the nights with somebody, makes room for sitting in silence, and keeps you eating and sleeping.

End of Life · Grief · Caregiving · Loss · 9 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Ask the team how long, and what to expect — not knowing is heavier than knowing.
  • Say the thing you would regret not saying — it does not have to be a speech.
  • Find out what they want and write it down — wishes are easier to honor in writing.
  • Take the night shifts in turns with someone — nobody can hold this alone for weeks.
  • Sit without talking sometimes — presence asks less of them than conversation does.
  • Eat and sleep on something like a schedule — you are no use to them running on nothing.
  • Keep 988 in your phone for the worst nights — call or text, any time, free across the United States.
  • Let other people do the practical things — somebody else can field the calls and the food.
  • Say goodbye more than once — there is no single right moment, and rarely the one you pictured.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
